headline: Compact CpG selection and memory-limited active learning for predictive biochemistry
label: Predictive Models For Biomolecular Data
summary: Recent work targets leaner models: fewer CpG features, pruned training data, and retention-time prediction from molecular descriptors.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned models that retain predictive performance while reducing the features or training data they require. MOSurvivor jointly selects CpG sites and tunes XGBoost through multi-objective search, reducing features by 79% at near-baseline epigenetic age-prediction error. SMAL removes training data during active learning and is benchmarked on six ADMET datasets and virtual-screening tasks. FastRet predicts LC-MS retention times from molecular descriptors using LASSO and boosted regression trees, packaged as an R tool. The set is heterogeneous: only MOSurvivor addresses omics data, while the other two address small-molecule property and chromatographic prediction. What is new is explicit parsimony as a design goal, whether in feature sets, training sets, or descriptor-based models, assessed against benchmark accuracy.
